svg.text: A SAR collection samples k-space on a POLAR grid: each pulse is an arc at constant aspect angle, each sample along
a pulse steps outward in range frequency. The 2-D FFT is only valid on a UNIFORM RECTANGULAR grid. Everything
in stages 1-2 exists to get from the left picture to the right one.
Radial spacing is set by df and the pulse's own
x0 -- which differ pulse to pulse, so the arcs
are neither concentric in index nor evenly
spaced. Hence a resample, not a reindex.
Uniform in both axes, so a separable 2-D FFT applies
and the hardware can do two 1-D passes with a
transpose between. The corner-turn between the
passes exists for exactly this reason.
